title: the Shiva Purana (selections)
hook: Daksha holds a great sacrifice and leaves out one guest, his own son-in-law Shiva, and his daughter Sati decides to go anyway

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Shiva Purana's pillar of fire, and the god honest enough to say: I couldn't find the end.
screen: `I COULDN'T FIND THE END.` · `A SECOND SELECTION.`

segments.voice: From the slopes of Kailash, Sati sees them go by in the sky: gods and their wives, dressed for a celebration, all heading the same way. They're going to her father's house. Daksha, her father, is holding a great sacrifice, a yajna, and the guests are streaming in. Everyone, it seems, except Sati and her husband. Daksha has left out his own son-in-law, Shiva. Sati turns to her husband and says she wants to go. A family quarrel that shakes the world.
screen: `GUESTS IN THE SKY.` → `EVERYONE BUT SHIVA.` → `SATI WANTS TO GO.`

segments.voice: The grudge is old. At an earlier gathering of the gods, Daksha walked in and the others rose to honor him, but Shiva stayed seated. Daksha took it as an insult. To him, Shiva was an embarrassment of a son-in-law: smeared with ash, wandering cremation grounds, no fine house. Shiva tells Sati plainly that going is a bad idea: to go where you haven't been invited brings dishonor, and her father means to insult them. But it's her father's house; surely her family won't turn her away. So she goes, and it's worse than Shiva said. There's no portion set aside for Shiva at all. Her father greets her coldly and speaks of her husband with contempt in front of everyone. Sati won't hear it. She rebukes her father before the gods, and then, the story says, she gives up her body by the power of her own yoga, rather than live as the daughter of the man who mocked Shiva. When word reaches Shiva, his grief becomes fury. From his matted hair he brings out Virabhadra, a terrible warrior, who storms the sacrifice and wrecks it. Daksha is killed. When the gods beg, Shiva relents, and Daksha is brought back to life with the head of a goat: a proud man, given a humbler face and a second chance. The story holds a lot of feeling, a daughter's loyalty, a husband's grief, a father's pride, and it treats contempt as no small thing: here, mockery brings down a great sacrifice. If a story like this stirs something heavy, or thoughts of harming yourself, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, or your local emergency number.
screen: `AN OLD GRUDGE AT A GATHERING.` · `SATI GOES ANYWAY.` · `SHE WILL NOT HEAR HIM MOCKED.` · `A GOAT'S HEAD AND A SECOND CHANCE.` · then, large: `A FAMILY QUARREL SHAKES THE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Let one old grudge come up, a slight, a time someone didn't stand up for you, or you for them, and without reliving it, notice how long you've carried it and where it sits in the body. On each out-breath, loosen your grip on it by one finger; you don't have to let it go today. If you pray, you can bring it to Shiva, or to God, in your own words.
The Shiva Purana. Today's selection: Daksha's sacrifice, where Sati would not hear her husband mocked.
Your line: the Shiva Purana, in selections. Even a proud father got a second chance. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus tell the story of Sati and Daksha's sacrifice in the Shiva Purana and other Puranas; Shaiva temples honor Virabhadra, and Sati's story is linked to the shakti pithas, places sacred to the goddess.
